back: Combines records from two or more tables by matching a related field, usually a foreign key with the primary key it refers to.
A query column worked out from other fields when the query runs, e.g. Quantity * UnitPrice AS LineTotal; it is not stored.
A query that prompts the user for a value each time it runs (e.g. [Enter town]) and uses it in its criteria.
Collects records sharing a value into groups and gives one result row per group, with SUM or COUNT for each.
SELECT … FROM A INNER JOIN B ON A.Key = B.Key WHERE …;

front: Steps for a program using a database
back: Connect, send SQL, read the results (loop), commit changes, close the connection.
An attack in which a user types SQL code into an input so that it changes the statement a program runs; prevented by passing input as parameters.
When two joined tables share a field name, write the table name and a dot first, e.g. Sales.ProductID.
